text:
Mika Zibanejad has three goals in 17 games, and only one in his last nine. Before reaching for his age (33), look at what he's getting. His chances add up to 3.97 expected goals, down to 0.68 per 60 minutes from 1.02 last season. That's a volume problem more than a finishing one. Thirty-one shots in 17 games is not the Zibanejad who came into the season with 348 career goals.

Some of it is bad luck around him. The Rangers have scored 4.6 fewer goals than their chances deserved with him on the ice, which has cost him points, and that usually swings back. At 5v5 they actually win the expected-goals battle with him out there (53%).

A Forever Blueshirts headline had him saying the Rangers "Played Disconnected Hockey in 3 Straight Games" late last month, and they have won their last two games. Our range still lands near 26 goals and 73 points. The thing to watch is shots: he's had more than three in just one of his last ten games.
headline: Zibanejad's quiet start is about shots, not finishing
